anomaly_def.Name: Replication Synchronization Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Replication Synchronization Anomaly : Standbys or downstream consumers cannot receive, write, or apply WAL/redo fast enough to keep pace with the primary, leading to growing replication lag and retention of log segments.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly : On-disk data or index pages become physically or logically corrupt, breaking key order, page links, or checksums and causing inconsistent query results or engine errors.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly : The database or log storage reaches or nears its physical or logical size limit, preventing further allocations or log recycling and causing allocation failures.

When all three root causes coexist, the system exhibits compounding symptoms: replication lag widens while retained primary log segments balloon; the enlarged log volume, unrecycled due to replica delay and corruption-triggered recovery retries, rapidly consumes remaining disk space until data files, archive areas, or temporary spaces hit hard limits. Corrupted pages or indexes surfaced on the replica may propagate back as apply failures, causing replication worker crashes, skipped transactions, or repeated retries that further increase lag. On the primary, space exhaustion and unrecycled logs generate "no space left" errors, stall checkpoints, and block new transactions, while read replicas deliver stale or inconsistent query results because of both replay delay and local corruption.

Causally, storage capacity pressure and replication backlogs reinforce each other: corruption encountered during replay forces replicas to halt or loop on failing records, which prevents log-position advancement; the primary therefore retains more WAL segments, accelerating space consumption. As free space dwindles, both primary and replica I/O subsystems may switch to synchronous archiving or halt allocations, further slowing write throughput and exacerbating replication lag. Simultaneously, corruption inside data or index pages can trigger larger redo generation (e.g., forced page writes or index rebuild attempts), inflating log volume when the replica is already behind. The intertwined feedback among replication delay, corruption-induced replay failures, and shrinking storage headroom drives the database toward a cascading failure that impairs availability, data integrity, and recovery options.

entry.official_description: All donors left. Aborting group replication incremental recovery.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with log shipping, replica apply state, replication-channel configuration, or cross-node communication needed to keep replicated state consistent.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect replication channel health, sender/receiver state, log retention, downstream apply lag, and network stability between replication endpoints.
